To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the current subprime mortgage crisis is a result of the failure of the financial services industry to regulate itself, and 2) the failure to regulate is a result of an absence of forbearance on the part of the industry.
the subprime mortgage crisis was caused by the interaction of a variety of factors including the government, the financial industry, the real estate industry, and the consumers.

(1) the subprime lending market has been characterized by a lack of forbearance, (2) forbearance is not likely to result from personal choices or regulatory efforts, and (3) grassroots efforts by users are necessary to ensure just outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to ensure economic justice for low-income communities.
the role that collective action can play in promoting economic justice in financial markets.
how the collective action of consumers can promote economic justice in the context of the subprime mortgage crisis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
forbearance is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a just society.

the subprime lending crisis can be prevented by collective efforts of users of financial services to promote forbearance among financial service providers and by regulatory efforts to promote forbearant behavior among users of financial services.
forbearance is a necessary condition of the invisible hand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that forbearance is a necessary condition to promote the common welfare in the context of real estate lending.
the collective action problem is not just a matter of information and incentive but also one of structure.
the subprime lending crisis has shown that the market for financial products and services has become a source of injustice for many low- and moderate-income people.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a grassroots movement is needed to ensure just real estate finance.
the collective action problem can be overcome by building on existing social capital.
the "invisible hand," which Smith described as the mechanism by which self-interested actions lead to social benefits, can only work if forbearance is exercised.
